correctness.rationale: Reconstructed definitions and proof: the glide g(i,j)=(i+m,n−1−j) and vertical period h produce a free properly discontinuous Klein-bottle deck group. Every nonidentity deck element displaces points by ≥min(m,n)≥7. A quotient clique of graph-distance ≤2 lifts uniquely within radius two of a chosen point; any wrong lift would be distance ≥7−4=3, so all lifted pairs have Manhattan distance ≤2. Such cliques fit exactly in 5-point radius-one stars or 4-point unit squares. Seven verified Git blobs reconstruct assigned record tree 9eaf840453be30b9a257414298f60c49c0e647b3. The five codimension-one free-face phases remove N,4N,N,N,2N pairs (N=mn), leaving precisely two chosen triangles per quotient unit square and the final f-vector (N,3N,2N). The quotient of the square cellulation under a glide is a Klein bottle, whose integral H1 is Z⊕Z/2 and whose higher H_i vanish. Independently implemented a networkx maximal-clique enumeration and every free-face deletion on twisted (7,7),(7,8),(8,9) and untwisted (7,7); all had the claimed f-vectors and exact 9N collapse lengths. Infinite assertion is proven by the uniform local proof, not finite enumeration. Boundary m=n=7 is within the displacement inequality; no assertion for dimensions <7 or other scales. A representative diagonal must be fixed consistently per quotient square, not assumed equivariant under orientation-reversing lifts.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge new result for orientation-reversing finite grid quotients with an explicit 9mn-pair elementary collapse. The Manhattan lattice star/square facet classification is already in Adams et al. Proposition 4.2, and is not credited as new. Its Theorem 5.8 is for the translation torus grid and gives a homotopy equivalence, not a Klein quotient or elementary simple-homotopy sequence. Related Resultary mathematical findings concern either the different open-neighborhood complex of toroidal translation quotients or width-four orientable Rips grids. No verified prior implication gives the complete present claim; broad generalized/unindexed lattice quotient literature remains a risk.
residual_risks: The local Manhattan star/square facet lemma was already published in Adams et al.; credit it as prior.

Saleh et al. and Adamaszek full documents were not independently re-read in this run; their abstracts did not present direct coverage. No whole-document absence claim is made.
Finite checker examples cannot certify all m,n; the universal assertion relies on the explicit lifting and free-face proof.

value.rationale: A sufficiently separated twisted square grid is a natural finite metric model of the nonorientable flat Klein bottle. Its inclusive scale-two Rips complex having integral Z/2 in H1, in contrast to the torsion-free torus grid, is a significant structural distinction; the explicit 9mn free-face sequence strengthens mere homotopy equivalence to a constructive simple-homotopy collapse uniformly in two grid parameters. This exact motivated fact is useful in discrete topology and metric sampling; no claim that m,n≥7 is the optimal lower cutoff.
